findings.text: Superblock naming helpers assign the stable sysfs identity from different origins such as attached block device identity, filesystem UUID content, informational identifier, or caller supplied formatted text with variable arguments. The UUID form expects full size UUID storage.

Inode release helper checks that the target is not freeing or clearing and that its reference count is positive, then drops one reference unless it is the last one. The outcome reports whether references remain.

User pathname helpers obtain a filename object from user memory, including a default flag wrapper and a nullable variant that honors empty path semantics and returns null only for absent input under that mode.

Character device helpers expose a simplified registration interface claiming a contiguous block of two hundred fifty six minors from zero for a given major and name, with a symmetric unregistration path.

File IO helpers wait for writeback over the entire file range, provide a default block mapping operation that always reports invalid argument, and perform block device direct IO bound to the owning device with interlock between buffered and direct paths and without hole filling.

Small predicates report executability from execute permission or directory type, type mismatch against file type bits, zero inode number from the low word, root identity by comparison with the mount root, dot and dotdot names by length and content, and empty path from descriptor validity and leading byte.

Superblock write helpers manage freeze protection at separate levels for regular writes, page faults and internal activity, offering blocking acquisition, nonblocking trylock acquisition and scoped release, plus a file level trylock that bypasses non regular files.

Encoding helpers expose the superblock unicode map, test its presence, compare two superblocks for version and flag compatibility, and validate strict casefolded names only when the directory is casefolded and strict encoding is enabled, otherwise accepting unconditionally.

Simple filesystem helpers provide a variable length argument response container, a no effect format validation placeholder used only for compiler checks, and macro generated attribute operations with selectable signed or unsigned write handling and standard open release read write and seek behavior.

Miscellaneous helpers include inert backing file security accessors, insertion of an inode into its hash by its own number, ownership or capability evaluation against the mount identity map, empty inode mutex key annotation, and a filesystem DAX mapping test that excludes device DAX character nodes and requires DAX support with an attached file.
Filename storage combines a header holding a string pointer with reference count and audit linkage together with an inline character store whose capacity completes a fixed total size.

Small helper structures include a delayed filename placeholder for an incomplete reference, a static tree descriptor with name operations and mode, an offset context with a tree plus next offset cursor, and a transaction response with size plus trailing payload.
Writer tracking for a superblock holds frozen state, separate kernel and userspace freeze counts, freeze owner identity, and a per level array of percpu semaphores sized by the freeze level count.

Superblock aggregates mount identity and lifecycle state including list linkage, device and type references, block sizing and file size bounds, operation vectors, mount and internal flags, magic, roots and mount lists, block and backing store links, quota data, writer freeze state, private data, time granularity and bounds, notification state, informational and stable names with UUID, link and dentry defaults, rename and sync serialization, subtype and dentry operations, shrinker and writeback lists, error sequencing, async completion and pin state, user namespace, LRU structures, RCU and teardown work, stack depth and inode list protection with randomized layout.

Superblock operation vector groups callbacks for inode allocation and lifecycle plus writeback, superblock teardown and synchronization, freeze and thaw at super and filesystem layers, statistics and unmount handling, option device path and stats display, quota IO, cache shrink accounting, device removal, shutdown and error reporting.
Freeze state advances from unfrozen through write freeze, page fault freeze, internal filesystem freeze, to completed freeze, with the usable level count derived from the completed value.
Freeze ownership distinguishes kernel and userspace holders and adds independent options permitting nesting and requesting exclusivity.

Writer protection selects the per level semaphore by level index offset, with dedicated release for page fault and internal levels and a file level fast path that grants immediately for non regular files without touching superblock state.
Directory relaxation requires holding the inode lock, drops and reacquires it in exclusive or shared mode, then reports liveness derived from dead directory state.

Size bounds derive maximum IO length from integer maximum masked to page granularity, inline filename capacity from fixed total minus header size, and transaction payload from page size minus header size.
Informational mount identity may evolve when device topology changes while the sysfs name stays stable for programmatic access, with sysfs visibility conditioned on that stable name.

Defensive behavior warns on UUID length mismatch when forming sysfs names, traps invalid release of freeing clearing or undercounted inodes, warns once on missing encoding for casefolded directories, and treats dead directories as failed relaxation.
Maximum read write length is integer maximum rounded down to page granularity.

Character major space has an overall cap of five hundred twelve, a normal dynamic endpoint at two hundred thirty four, and an extended dynamic interval from five hundred eleven down to three hundred eighty four.
Direct IO options use one for locking between buffered and direct access and two for skipping holes.

Mount option bits cover read only, ignore suid and device, disallow exec, synchronous writes, mandatory locks, synchronous directories, access time suppression for files and directories, silent operation, ACL support, inline encryption, kernel mount, version update, lazy time, dead and dying states, force, no security, born, active and no user.

Internal superblock bits cover cgroup writeback, exec and device suppression, stable writes, restricted variant, unverifiable signature, untrusted mounter, unsupported digest, skipped sync, per super backing device, timestamp expiry warned, retired, no umask, no idmap, HSM allowed and no data integrity.

Encoding option bits distinguish strict mode and no compat fallback, with fallback queries reporting compatibility disabled when unicode support is absent; freeze levels span zero to four with three usable writer levels.
Exec file mode constant is the forced integer form of the underlying exec mode value.

Dispatch entry points include a direct IO submission callback taking a bio and inode, and the superblock operation vector through which generic code invokes filesystem specific lifecycle sync freeze stat display and teardown behavior.
Headers use single inclusion guards for superblock helpers, superblock types and filesystem context definitions.
